notes.title: Open Beta Has Ended! A Thank You from Chief Rebel
notes.content: [p]Hello Fellows! [/p][p] [/p][p][b]The [i]Fellowship [/i]Open Beta has ended, and we want to extend our gratitude to all of you for traveling to the Stronghold and going on a slew of dungeon runs![/b] The main purpose of the Beta was to get one final round of feedback before [i]Fellowship[/i] launches on Steam in Early Access on October 16 – and you all definitely gave us a ton of great feedback and support. Thank you all for making the Open Beta a huge success, we really appreciate every single one of you who jumped in! We wish we could extend the Beta (know many of you have asked for that!), but we need to set our sights on getting [i]Fellowship[/i] ready for Early Access launch and implement all the great feedback you’ve given us.  [/p][p] [/p][p]We know the Open Beta had some server issues throughout, meaning so many of you decided to hop in and play. We’re sorry those issues came up, but we worked hard alongside Arc Games to closely monitor and address your reports to ensure you encountered less issues (and jumped into dungeons more quickly!) We’ve been able to identify ways to improve server stability across the board, and rest assured that for Early Access launch we hope to have the servers as stable as possible – so you all can focus on just having fun.  [/p][p] [/p][p]That said, we’re thrilled [i]so [/i]many of you got to try out [i]Fellowship[/i] during the Beta, and our Fellows got to play as Mara (you sneaky rogues) for the first time and experience the new gameplay systems we’ve implemented, including our new matchmaking and group finding systems. Many content creators, including [u][url="https://www.twitch.tv/shroud"]Shroud[/url][/u], [u][url="https://twitch.tv/guzu"]GuzuTV[/url][/u], [u][url="https://twitch.tv/xaryu"]Xaryu[/url][/u], and more, along with [i]World of Warcraft[/i] guilds, including Liquid, Echo and Method, partnered with us and streamed [i]Fellowship[/i], as they squaded up with friends and took on some of the most challenging dungeons.  [/p][p] [/p][p]We loved watching all of you discover your favorite heroes, dungeon strats, and epic gear during the Beta – and we absolutely can’t wait for all you to play the game more in just a few weeks. For now, we’ll be hard at work (and catching up on sleep along the way) to implement your feedback and create a fuller experience for when [i]Fellowship [/i]launches on Steam in[i] [/i]Early Access! Make sure to continue to tune into our [url="https://discord.gg/playfellowship"]Discord[/url] and social channels for updates leading up to Early Access launch, including new trailers.  [/p][p] [/p][p]We look forward to you all jumping into [i]Fellowship[/i] again pretty soon when the game releases on Steam in Early Access on October 16! [/p][p][/p][p]Cheers,[/p][p]Chief Rebel[/p]

notes.title: Open Beta Now Live!
notes.content:
[p][previewyoutube=SnsHsUrbeuc;full][/previewyoutube][/p][p][b]Fellowship’s Open Beta via Steam is NOW LIVE! Join the Beta today![/b]

Jump in the Beta by clicking on the “Join the Playtest” button on Fellowship’s Steam page. The Beta is available to everyone (yes, everyone!) and we have it running 24/7 every day from now until Tuesday, September 23 at 10am PT. Don’t miss your chance to see how Fellowship has evolved since its last public playtest. Check out the below Open Beta FAQ before you jump in the Beta. 

After our last public playtest during Steam Next Fest back in February – and landing a top 5 spot in the “[url="https://store.steampowered.com/sale/nextfestmostplayed_feb_2025"]Steam Next Fest: Most-Played Demos[/url]” list (thanks to you all!) – we’re thrilled to launch the Fellowship Open Beta on Steam today! With your help in multiple closed playtests over the past months the game has evolved a lot, and this Open Beta will be one more opportunity to get your community feedback before we enter Early Access on October 16th. We hope you’ll have a ton of fun playing, and we’re looking forward to your feedback [url="https://discord.gg/playfellowship"]on our Fellowship Discord[/url].

We’ll see you in-game in the Beta, Fellows! 

Don’t forget, Fellowship will be available on Steam in Early Access on October 16 for $24.99. Make sure to wishlist the game today!

[/p][h3][b]Open Beta FAQ[/b][/h3][p][b]There really is no signup, payment or key required?[/b] [/p][p]Correct, there is no need to sign up, key or fee required for the Open Beta! It's open to everyone!  [/p][p][b]How do I get into the Open Beta?[/b] [/p][p]During the time of Open Beta from September 18 to September 23, you can head to Fellowship’s Steam page, click the “Join the Fellowship Playtest” to download the Open Beta build, and once it’s downloaded, you can jump in and play.  [/p][p][b]When can I play exactly?[/b] [/p][p]The Open Beta runs from today, September 18 at 10am PT (7pm CEST) to September 23 at 10 am PT (7pm CEST) and Fellowship will be fully playable for that whole time.  [/p][p][b]Can I stream/capture my gameplay?[/b] [/p][p]There is no NDA for this Open Beta. Streaming/video capture and talking about the playtest is highly encouraged!  [/p][p][b]What's ArcLite? It popped up when I clicked "Play" on Steam to go into the Beta.[/b][/p][p]ArcLite is the launcher for [i]Fellowship[/i]. Through ArcLite, you can access the latest news, events, rewards, and community updates—all focused around [i]Fellowship[/i]. Please see the ArcLite FAQ below for more details on ArcLite.[/p][p][b]What Heroes are available?[/b] There are 7 heroes for players to choose from during the Open Beta: 2 Tanks, 3 DPS, and 2 Healers. We’ll most notably have a new Melee DPS, Mara, available, and be bringing back Ardeos, everyone’s favorite fire-throwing DPS! Tariq is not available in this Beta. [/p][p][b]Is there any new content in the Open Beta compared to the last playtest back in February?[/b] [/p][p]There is! Compared to the Steam Next Fest demo back in February, in addition to introducing a new DPS hero, Mara, the Open Beta introduces new gameplay systems, including a fresh take on matchmaking and group finding, and an engaging progression system including Weapons, Gems, Talents, Crafting, Legendary items and more. Additionally, the Open Beta introduces a new dungeon “Urrak Markets”, new gameplay features like cosmetic customization allowing you to change the look of different pieces of armor, new Gear, new Mounts, new visual element improvements and improvements on previous gameplay mechanics based on Steam Next Fest player feedback. The Open Beta allows us to test multiplayer matchmaking improvements we’ve made and give us the chance to get one final round of player feedback before Fellowship’s Early Access launch.  [/p][p][b]What servers are available?[/b][/p][p]There are NA, EU, and Asian servers available during the Open Beta.  [/p][p][b]Will my Open Beta progress carry over to the Early Access version of the game?[/b][/p][p]It will not. [/p][p][b]What languages are the Open Beta available in?[/b] [/p][p]The Open Beta is available in English, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Korean, and Chinese. The game will launch in your chosen Steam language or default to English if it’s not supported.  [/p][p][b]How do I share my feedback?[/b] [/p][p][url="https://discord.gg/playfellowship"]Join our Discord![/url] Feedback can be shared in the ⁠#game-feedback channel. Through ArcLite, you can access the latest news, events, rewards, and community updates—all focused around [i]Fellowship[/i].[/p][p][b]Will ArcLite run in the background while I’m playing the game?[/b][/p][p]No. Once you launch [i]Fellowship[/i] through ArcLite, the launcher will automatically close.[/p][p][b]Heard there's an in-game award I can get through ArcLite? What is the reward and how do I get it?[/b][/p][p]The reward is for [i]Fellowship[/i] players who verify their email when opening ArcLite. Simply enter your email address, complete the verification process, and the reward will be granted to you. The reward is an exclusive in-game mount, Arcalian Steed (check it out below!) [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45129917/39beed6c41d553afaa9e56622c06df4708b202bc.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Will this reward carry over to the Early Access version of the game?[/b][/p][p]The reward will automatically be re-granted to your account when you purchase the Early Access version of the game. Will it interfere with ArcLite?[/b][/p][p]No. ArcLite and Arc are independent applications and do not interfere with each other.[/p][p][b]I'm running into technical difficulties. Where do I seek support?[/b][/p][p]You can click the [b]Support[/b] option under the Arc icon in the top left corner of ArcLite, or simply visit [/p][p][url="https://support.arcgames.com"]support.arcgames.com[/url] to create a support ticket.[/p][p][/p][p]Follow: [url="https://x.com/Play_Fellowship"]https://x.com/Play_Fellowship[/url] [/p][p]Watch: [dynamiclink href="https://www.twitch.tv/PlayFellowship"][/dynamiclink] [/p][p]YouTube: [dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/@PlayFellowship"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]Like: [url="https://www.facebook.com/FellowshipGame"]https://www.facebook.com/FellowshipGame[/url] [/p][p]Discuss: [url="https://discord.gg/playfellowship"]https://discord.gg/playfellowship[/url][/p]

notes.title: Early Access Launch Update
notes.content:
[previewyoutube="yBlcVdX5siY;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Hi Fellows!

We’ve got an update for you regarding our planned Steam Early Access release date for Fellowship. In the video linked above, Community Director Hamish explains the release date update, upcoming changes and dives into a few other important topics!

[b]In case you’re in a hurry, here’s a summary of the video and a few additional notes:[/b]

[b]Steam Early Access Launch Date:[/b] We’ve made the decision to push back the release date by one week. 
[/p][p][h3]You'll be able to play Fellowship in Steam Early Access on October 16th instead of October 9th![/h3]

We know you all want to jump in the game ASAP (trust us, we can’t wait for you all to jump in!), but there are a couple of key reasons for this very small shift with the Early Access release date:

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45129917/a39d794433e112ae2269e9bfb72e8dd18654cdf0.jpg"][/img][/p][p][i][b]More time for changes & polish[/b]:[/i] The slight delay gives us the opportunity to put in extra polish and ensure the best possible experience for you all on day one when Fellowship enters Steam Early Access! As you all know, we’ve been having our private playtest recently – which has helped us identify changes we can make to the game. Having some additional development time, even if it's only a week (a week goes a long way!) will allow us to make the changes and polish we want to make so Fellowship is the best it can be when it enters Early Access on October 16th!  [/p][p][/p][p][i][b]To address the elephant in the room[/b] – we want to give Fellowship it’s time to shine[/i]: There are major game releases happening the week we originally planned to enter Early Access. Following Gamescom, we saw your all’s concerns about launching Fellowship during a major week for highly-anticipated game releases and recognized of course you all (like us!) wanted to make sure Fellowship has its time to shine in the spotlight. We always want to be transparent with our community and get your feedback, and this is no different! By launching Fellowship in Steam Early Access on October 16, it allows us to make sure the game does get in the spotlight and get the attention we and you all think it deserves!

[b]Open Beta – No changes:[/b] No changes here, we absolutely can’t wait for you all to jump in! The Open Beta via Steam will still kick off on Thursday, September 18 at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time and end on Tuesday, September 23 at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time. For the Open Beta, there will be a North America, Europe and Asia server available, and servers will be online 24/7! You can request access to the Open Beta via the game’s Steam page to be notified immediately when the Open Beta goes live.

At the very end of this blog, we have an Open Beta FAQ with quite a few answers to questions folks have asked since we announced the Beta. Make sure to check it out!

[b]Leagues System & Matchmaking Updates:[/b] The Leagues System will be a new way to experience progression throughout Fellowship! With the system, you’ll be able to make your way through different leagues as your experience, gear, and item level improves. Matchmaking will set you up with players of similar item level, and you will then be able to pick a dungeon of suitable difficulty. Prepare to complete dungeon runs, enter higher leagues, and reap exciting rewards!

Our matchmaking game modes will remain about the same but will have some quality-of-life changes to make matchmaking even better. For modes, we’ll have Quick Play, and for now, what we’re calling Challenge (previously known as Ranked or Ranked Dungeons). Quick Play, like before, offers a more casual experience that’d give you a chance to try out new heroes, and not have to worry about gear as your gear will not matter but you’ll of course still have all your usual abilities per character! Our Challenge mode (name to be decided!), will have the Leagues System and really dive deep into the game’s progression, as you’ll work your way up to harder difficulty dungeons. The higher the league you’re in, the more challenging and rewarding dungeons will be!

[b]Localization:[/b] Right at Steam Early Access launch on October 16, Fellowship will be playable in the following languages: English, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Korean, and Chinese! The game will launch in your chosen Steam language or default to English if it’s not supported.

[b]Fellowship Content from Creators:[/b] Leading up to our Open Beta and during the beta, you’ll be able to watch some of your favorite creators play Fellowship on Twitch and YouTube. Beyond Open Beta, there’ll be even more content from press and content creators to be shared before, on and even after Early Access launch. Keep an eye on our social media channels and join our Discord to not miss out on anything!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45129917/636ac1b9229b99365b2113b864778af867766c6d.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Open Beta FAQ[/b][/h3][p]If you made it this far, thanks for sticking around! Below’s a quick FAQ addressing some questions we spotted since we announced the Beta. We’ll share this FAQ again when the Open Beta launches, so no need to memorize it!

[b]There really is no signup, payment or key required?[/b]
Correct, there is no need to sign up, key or fee required for the Open Beta! It’ll be open to everyone!

[b]How do I get into the Open Beta?[/b]
During the time of Open Beta from September 18 to September 23, you can head to Fellowship’s Steam page, click the “Join the Fellowship Playtest” to download the Open Beta build, and once it’s downloaded, you can jump in and play. 

If you’d like immediately to know when the Beta is live (or just need a friendly reminder!), you can request access now via Fellowship’s Steam page.

[b]When can I play exactly?[/b]
The Open Beta runs from September 18 at 10am PT (7pm CEST) to September 23 at 10 am PT (7pm CEST) and Fellowship will be fully playable for that whole time.

[b]Can I stream/capture my gameplay?[/b]
There will be no NDA for this Open Beta. Streaming/video capture and talking about the playtest is highly encouraged!

[b]What Heroes are available?[/b]
There will be 7 heroes for players to choose from during the Open Beta: 2 Tanks, 3 DPS, and 2 Healers. We’ll most notably have a new Melee DPS, Mara, available, and be bringing back Ardeos, everyone’s favorite fire-throwing DPS! 

[b]Will there be any new content in the Open Beta compared to the last playtest back in February?[/b]
There will be! Compared to the Steam Next Fest demo back in February, in addition to introducing a new DPS hero, Mara, the Open Beta will introduce new gameplay systems, including a fresh take on matchmaking and group finding, and an engaging progression system including Weapons, Gems, Talents, Crafting, Legendary items and more. Additionally, the Open Beta will introduce a new dungeon “Urrak Markets”, new gameplay features like cosmetic customization allowing you to change the look of different pieces of armor, new Gear, new Mounts, new visual element improvements and improvements on previous gameplay mechanics based on Steam Next Fest player feedback. The Open Beta will allow us to test multiplayer matchmaking improvements we’ve made and give us the chance to get one final round of player feedback before Fellowship’s Early Access launch.

[b]Will there be servers in my region? [/b]
There are NA, EU, and Asian servers available during the Public Playtest.

[b]What languages are the Open Beta available in?[/b]
We are planning to have the Open Beta available in English, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Korean, and Chinese.

[b]How do I share my feedback?[/b]
[url="https://discord.gg/playfellowship"]Join our Discord![/url] Feedback can be shared in the ⁠#game-feedback channel.

[b]What do I do if I encounter an issue during the Open Beta?[/b]
As this is still a Beta build, you may occasionally encounter issues with your game. If you do, please report them in the ⁠#bug-reports ⁠channel on Discord so our teams can track them.

notes.title: Fellowship Launches In Early Access On October 16!
notes.content:
[h3][b]We’re excited to announce that Fellowship will be available on Steam in Early Access on October 16, 2025 for $24.99. 

Before Early Access launch, you’ll be able to play during our Open Beta via Steam from September 18 until September 23![/b] [/h3][p][/p][h3][b]ABOUT EARLY ACCESS[/b][/h3][p]The upcoming Early Access launch will mark just the beginning of Fellowship, as the game will be a constantly evolving adventure with a slew of content that will be added and evolve thanks to YOUR feedback throughout the course of Early Access. Our community comes first, and we take pride in working very closely with our most dedicated fans to create and shape the game over the various stages of development.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45129917/4fdaec1d4676bb5be527325a38b2824d332a6de6.jpg"][/img]From the very beginning of Early Access, you will be able to experience the core vision of Fellowship: all dungeons, all the time – giving you the action you want right from the start. Following Early Access launch, there are plans for optional cosmetic purchases to be available. We'd like to make clear that these items will be purely cosmetic and not affect gameplay. More details on these items will be revealed sometime closer to Early Access launch.

Fellowship is planned to be in Early Access for approximately six months, but this can change depending on your feedback – as we will strive to discover what the community wants in Fellowship to help shape it into the best possible game it can be before it enters 1.0 launch next year. For the full 1.0 version of the game, we're planning on including more content, systems, and features. We have several plans in mind for content and features, but as mentioned before, we will also take your feedback to heart and may make adjustments if we hear that there’s something you really want to see in the game!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45129917/9beccea2429425d0333f34ed82645e33c1153127.jpg"][/img]Compared to the Steam Next Fest demo back in February, in addition to introducing a new DPS hero, Mara, the Open Beta will introduce new gameplay systems, including a fresh take on matchmaking and group finding, and an engaging progression system including Weapons, Gems, Talents, Crafting, Legendary items and more. notes.title: Developer Update: Public Playtest Wrap-Up & What’s Next
notes.content:
Hi Fellows! 

It’s been just a little over a month since our Public Playtest (demo) for Steam Next Fest – which ICYMI went extremely well to say the least (see the infographic below) – but we wanted to take a moment to share a Developer Update video that addresses your playtest feedback, how we plan to improve Fellowship based on the feedback and what’s next for the game as we get it ready for Early Access launch. Be sure to check out the video as it has a few things we’ve been working on lately based on your feedback! 

[previewyoutube=c9zv5T6l-tQ;full][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45129917/877a7834db0ad7db3e8c830ea08b068006139a41.jpg[/img]

We’ll be spending the next few months focused on developing Fellowship, but don’t worry, we won’t be silently working.  We will still be giving you all updates as we continue development. Updates will include sharing news (yes, that includes news of the Early Access release date – we’ll have news on that when we’re ready!), videos/trailers, dev team blogs, and last but certainly not least giving you all a chance to take a look on what we’re working on along the way.  

Aside from giving wider updates, we also have our Fellowship Community Council, our new community program where we’ve hand-picked and will continue to hand-pick a group of players – from competitive players to players that are new to this type of game, and give these players the chance to connect directly with us! For the program, folks that are in it can get exclusive access to in-development builds of Fellowship (under NDA, of course) and give us feedback in real-time to shape the future of our game. If you’re interested in joining the council, send Hamish, our Community Director, a DM via Discord, share with him why you’d be a good fit, and he’ll make sure to add you to the list for consideration to join the council. 

That’s it for today’s dev update, but we’re thrilled to continue development on Fellowship after all the incredible feedback we got from you all from the Public Playtest! We can’t wait to share more updates as we work on getting Fellowship ready for Early Access launch later this year.  

Cheers, 

Chief Rebel Team

notes.title: A Thank You from Chief Rebel
notes.content:
Hi Fellows!

Now that we’ve reached the end of our first Public Playtest for [i]Fellowship[/i], we wanted to take a moment to stop and thank everyone that tried out our pride and joy. 

We’ve known for a long time that we’ve got something very special here with [i]Fellowship[/i] but for the first time, we were able to see exactly how players truly feel about our game. The truth? We’re blown away by the response. 

It’s been incredible watching players at the bleeding edge push [i]Fellowship[/i] to the absolute limit but we’ve also been buoyed by the smaller stories; players reaching out because they’d tried our game on a whim having never experienced this kind of gameplay before and absolutely falling in love. We’ve had emails from people wanting to make plushies, incredible fan art for proposed heroes, actual theorycrafting sims and so much more. You’d be forgiven for thinking this test had been running for months but all of these incredible things have happened in the space of only ten days. We couldn’t have dreamed of a better response and the team are hyped beyond belief to show you what comes next. 

Because this test went so well, it’s easy to forget that this was just a dress rehearsal. The reality is that we’re only at the start of what we believe to be a long and exciting road for [i]Fellowship[/i]. You don’t even need to take our word for it, we’ve heard you and we know that the feeling is mutual.

With that, we have one last thing to ask you: don’t go anywhere. Stay tuned to all of our channels as we bring you news of what’s coming next and all of the important things we’ve learnt from you during this test. Now it’s time for our team at Chief Rebel and Arc Games to fix our sleep schedules which you’ve ruined from all the sleepless nights watching you play and talk about [i]Fellowship[/i]! We’re not mad about it and we can’t wait to do it all over again.

Much love,
Chief Rebel

[h2]Known Issues[/h2]

[h3]Friends List - “how do I group up with my friends?”
[/h3]
The only way to group up with your friends when in different strongholds - is to use Fellowship’s in-game Friends List feature.
[list]
[*] The Friends List is the green icon in the bottom right corner of your screen.
[*] Add friends by using the Friend Code generated in the Fellowship’s Friend’s List feature. For this build, you will need to send that code to your friend using an external chat program.
[*] The Friends List does not indicate that players are outside of your region. Party members playing in different regions will never be put into the same Stronghold. When starting a mission, all players in a party will be put into a dungeon server in the Party Leaders region. This can lead to high ping or latency issues if the host is playing in a different region than you.
[*] The Friends List will display your friend as offline if they are not in the game or logged. (Ignores Steam)
[*] Friends List uses a placeholder hero icon until a friend switches heroes.
[*] Friends List will use a generic Fellowship icon if it cannot access the player’s Steam icon.
[/list]

[h3]Party[/h3]
[list]
[*] Party Frames do not update to include players outside of your Stronghold server. Reference the big ‘Party Portraits’ in the top left corner of your screen while you are in the Stronghold for the source of truth for who is in your party.
[*] It is possible to be invited to a new party while currently in a party. Accepting the invite will remove you from your current party.
[/list]

[h3]Game Finder[/h3]
[list]
[*] Players can find/host a Dungeon at a difficulty below the unlock difficulty level.
[*] This can lead to long waits for Dungeon queues, because players on lower difficulties cannot access those dungeons.
[*] We suggest players find/host dungeons at higher difficulties than they are unlocked at. 
[*] Cithrel’s Ascent (+3)
[*] Demonbrand Ruins (+4)
[*] Wraithtide Isle (+6)
[*] Potential Rewards will suggest that Set Items can drop from Adventures. They do not.
[*] Next Unlock section will vanish when there is not an Unlock for completing the next available difficulty.
[*] Button Glows seem to ‘hop’ up when clicked.
[*] Premade groups cannot play quickplay if they defy holy trinity party composition (1 Tank, 1 Healer, 2 Damage Dealers). Groups wanting to make experimental party comps should ‘Host Game’ with a full group. 
[*] 
[/list]

[h3]Settings[/h3]
Graphic Settings

[*] With this, Graphic Settings will automatically apply (Apply and Cancel do nothing).
[*] Auto-Detect button cannot be trusted to detect the ideal Graphic Settings for you. Do not use it!
[/list]

[h3]Talent Tree[/h3]

[*] This can lead to several instances of UI existing simultaneously behind each other.

notes.title: Dev Interview: André
notes.content:
This week, André takes center stage in our dev interview. Let’s hear what he’s up to at Chief Rebel and let’s try to get another sneak peek at what’s being cooked!

[b]Q: Who are you and what do you do at Chief Rebel?[/b]
A: Hello! My name is André Boström, and I work as Art Director at Chief Rebel, more specifically I am the Art Director on Fellowship. My key responsibility is to set the art direction on Fellowship and execute on that vision together with our talented team of artists. We have various sub-crafts I work with daily: Concept Art, 3D Art, Character Art, VFX, Animation and UI Art. I work with the other directors to ensure we’re building the right game together.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45129917/bed902bdc8eae35c14817ad77ae58c29018a11f6.jpg[/img]
[b]Q: How did you find your way to Chief Rebel?[/b]
A: I started out as an indie developer back in 2008 and always dreamed of working on stylized games. After many years of AAA development, I felt a yearning to return to my roots. Working with dedicated and focused teams on passion projects always felt like my calling. I sought out this role because I grew up playing the types of games we want to develop at Chief Rebel. I felt like I connected with what the studio wanted to do on a deeper level, and I very much wanted to be a part of realizing that vision.

[b]Q: What’s the best part about working for Chief Rebel?[/b]
A. The best part about working for Chief Rebel is having the honor to work together with kind, talented and like-minded individuals, on our very own creative work. It is a privilege to carve a footprint and help pave the way for more stylized games.

[b]Q: Do you have any advice for those who want to work in the industry that you can share with the community?[/b]
A: I think the most salient advice I can give is to ‘go for it’. When I first started working with games all I knew was that I wanted to continue making art! Look inward and see if there is something which speaks to you with regards to games specifically: is it animation, audio, narrative, design, gameplay, etc. which speaks to you? From there I’d say the next steps would be to look at how you can get involved with the games community. In certain places nowadays there are even programs you can enroll in to learn game development skills. These did not really exist when I started out and I’m constantly impressed by the work I see from students. In short: Look for what speaks to you, and then go for it. Start making things. Don’t be scared to fail. We all fail - learning is a lifelong journey. Take one step at a time and embrace the process. I believe in you!

[b]Q: What are your typical tasks and responsibilities on a normal day at Chief Rebel?[/b]
A: I come into the office each morning and say good morning to our wonderful Iti at the reception. Then I’ll sync with the other directors on the project about what we’re doing that day. Typically, I’ll then take a walk around the office and look at the work the art department is up to, moving across the team, talking to our artists, supporting and helping them out where I can. I will help out with concept art, do various art related tasks and engage in project planning as well. This is also an opportunity for me to learn and develop our workflows and also hone my own skills. Ultimately, the majority of my time is spent maintaining the visual identity of Fellowship.

[b]Q: Can you give us a sneak peek of what you’re working on right now?[/b]
A: Here is a sneak peek concept art I'm working on for one of our heroes, Mara.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45129917/f748682ca48b28d39510b17ba46e3f75ed5ea010.jpg[/img]
[b]Q: Who is Mara?[/b]
A: Mara is a deadly assassin with a shadowy past. She weaves in and out of the darkness with precision and may even be able to change her form to slash at her foes!

[b]Q: What other games or media do you draw inspiration from?[/b]
A: I’ve been playing games all of my life, but I draw inspiration from all kinds of places, be it games, films, books etc. I’ve been fortunate enough to have parents, friends and a partner who have all indulged me in my interests, so I’ve been able to build a sizable library of references throughout my life thus far. As far as Fellowship goes, we draw inspiration primarily from western RPGs and games a lot of us grew up with: MMORPGs, RPGs, ARPGs, MOBAs, etc.

[b]Q: What’s your first gaming memory?[/b]
A: I don’t have a specific memory in mind, but playing SNES, Gameboy and Dreamcast with my siblings immediately comes to mind. Sitting in front of (what we thought then) a huge CRT until our eyes essentially became square-shaped and bit-soup running out of my ears are fond memories of mine. My first memory playing computer games (Commodore 64 is a blur), however, goes back to Captain Claw. It’s a little-known gem by Monolith Productions, and incidentally one of my favorite games of all time. Here is a picture of me playing the demo on my dad’s computer back in 1997, begging to get the full game for the holidays!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45129917/08a6433cc0a4467f5677f8567caefd17db680e52.jpg[/img]
[b]Q: What are you doing when you’re not working on Fellowship? Any hobbies or activities you want to share with us?[/b]
A: I like learning new things, though some activities have stuck with me longer than others. I play bass guitar from time to time. I also practice Karate and have done so for over a decade now. I like to write, and I have been working on a personal project for what feels like forever - maybe one day I will get to realize it into some type of game - for now I paint concept art and write to store my ideas for that project. I am also interested in people and behavior and enjoy philosophy in general. Otherwise, I like to simply spend quality time with my partner and family with the time I’m given.

notes.title: Dev Interview: Thea
notes.content:
Thea makes up half of our VFX team here at Chief Rebel and works on all the super-satisfying, shiny, pretty things that make Fellowship both satisfying to play and awesome to look at. We asked her a bunch of questions, but it was also a great excuse to track down some footage of a never-before-seen boss. Sorry, spoilers.

[b]Q: Who are you and what do you do at Chief Rebel?[/b]
A: My name is Thea and I’m a VFX artist.

[b]Q: How did you find your way to Chief Rebel?[/b]
A: They actually found me! I was studying at Futuregames and there was a meet and greet week planned with a bunch of different gaming companies. Chief Rebel reached out to me the week before the meet and greet, said they liked my portfolio and asked if I was willing to meet with them. I initially hesitated because at the time there was zero info available on the company and the website only had their logo on it. But I got this gut feeling that I should talk to them anyway, and I’m so glad I did. I was sold from the very first interview.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45129917/c4778db2492a71c6e6dafb87d3baf63b8602b95f.jpg[/img]
[b]Q: What’s the best part about working for Chief Rebel?[/b]
A: The team! We work hard on building trust and thanks to that, this is the first company where I’ve felt that I can truly be myself and that’s everything to me.

[b]Q: Do you have any advice for those who want to work in the industry that you can share with the community?[/b]
A: Figure out what discipline you are the most passionate about, and what types of games you want to do. Then look at how games in that genre do it and learn from that. If you can, get a mentor from the industry to help you out. Be prepared that it can take some time to get a foot in the door, so make sure your portfolio is great and try to get as many industry contacts as you can.

[b]Q: What are your typical tasks and responsibilities on a normal day at Chief Rebel?[/b]
A: I’m responsible for the Dungeon VFX. That includes bosses, enemies and some environment VFX. I work closely with the rest of the dungeon team to ensure that you will have a great time fighting our enemies!

I'm also mentoring our newest VFX artist, creating technical solutions and new processes to improve how we do all the VFX in Fellowship.

[b]Q: Can you give us a sneak peek of what you’re working on right now?[/b]
A: I’m working on a really cool boss for an upcoming dungeon and, even though we haven't showed it yet, I'm told that it's ok if I share this and I definitely won't get in trouble.

[previewyoutube=cWDU-sfWG2M;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]Q: What other games or media do you draw inspiration from?[/b]
A: I take inspiration from WoW, LoL, and various talented artists on Art Station. I also take inspo from movies and TV series. For example, when I created the shadow VFX kit, I took inspiration from Claire's shadow magic in Trollhunters and the idea for how the soul kit should look came from dementors in Harry Potter.

But to be honest, most of the time I just feel randomly inspired and get a feeling, a vibe, that I just roll with.

[b]Q: What’s your first gaming memory?[/b]
A: Getting in trouble for sneaking up in the middle of the night to play Tetris Plus with my big brother when I was around 4 years old. It’s a PS1 game and it’s like normal Tetris, with one of the best soundtracks I’ve heard (yes even to this day). It's set in ancient ruins and there’s this little archaeologist dude on the top row that will get crushed by a pike trap if the Tetris blocks get too high. The goal was to get him to fall down a gap to the button and in VS mode it was a race against each other, which always led to some intense sibling rivalry and us making a whole bunch of noise. Mom was super strict about what games we played and for how long until we were in our teens so, at the time, we were allowed no more than 30 min/day. Getting caught in the middle of the night got us in a lot of trouble and we weren't allowed to play anything for a week. Totally worth it though!

[b]Q: What are you doing when you’re not working on Fellowship? Any hobbies or activities you want to share with us?[/b]
A: I play outrageous amounts of Cities Skylines 2, draw on my iPad, and hang out with friends and family.

notes.title: Announcing: Fellowship
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=BuhVdx9K0Fc;full][/previewyoutube]

We’re excited to announce Fellowship, the first-ever multiplayer online dungeon adventure (“MODA”) game. Fellowship is developed by Chief Rebel, a new game studio based in Stockholm, Sweden with industry veterans who’ve worked on critically-acclaimed video game franchises. With Fellowship, it will take fan-favorite elements of MMOs, MOBAs and ARPGs, including thrilling endgame dungeon runs, a diverse roster of heroes, cooperative, team-focused gameplay and epic loot, to give players a truly unique and challenging yet accessible PvE dungeon crawling experience. Fellowship will be a premium, not free-to-play or subscription-based title and is set to launch on PC in 2025.

There will be a Closed Alpha playtest on Steam from August 15 to 20, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2352620/view/4324103463976799109]find out all details and how to sign up in this article[/url]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45129917/64071f92c4ecbd4e63ab59d1833d6b0c8d8bec82.jpg[/img]
[h3]ABOUT FELLOWSHIP[/h3]

Fellowship is a multiplayer online dungeon adventure set in an exciting fantasy setting, with endlessly scaling dungeon runs. Players must focus on working together as a team, with an emphasis on skill, cooperation, and strategy to defeat bosses, collect loot, and work together to overcome ever-present challenges. Experience the “Holy Trinity” and build the ultimate team of tanks, healers and damage dealers to take down hordes of enemies and imposing bosses. Work together with your friends to overcome the greatest challenges, creating unbreakable bonds and memorable moments. Players can also flex their individual skills on the competitive leaderboards that show where you stand in Fellowship. Persevere, overcome and ascend through the top ranks in Fellowship!

[h3]GAME FEATURES[/h3]

[b]GATHER YOUR PERFECT TEAM[/b] - Play alongside your friends in teams with 4 Player Co-op Multiplayer in a rich, fantasy world full of challenging enemies and exciting rewards. Swap between a large pool of tank, healer and DPS roles with unique kits to build the perfect balance for your team.

[b]ENDLESS SCALING REPLAYABILITY[/b] - Every run will feel like a brand-new challenge with dungeons that will get more difficult as players progress and level up. Players will never out level the game with seasonal updates, dungeon modifiers, new features and rewards that will keep each run fresh and exciting, adding another layer of replayability.

[b]UNIQUE AND COMPLEX BOSS MECHANICS[/b] - Each boss has unique and varied mechanics, for a fresh experience every run. Enemy skills grow as difficulty increases and additional modifiers continue to challenge players as they grow and improve.

[b]REWARDS, LOOT, AND GEAR GALORE[/b] - After each completed dungeon run, players will earn loot to make their characters even more powerful! The tougher the dungeon, the better the rewards.
